sections.title: A collection that *outgrew the house*

image.alt: A wide view of the arcade floor and its rows of machines

body: Owners Eric and Erin are long-time Aiken residents who started collecting pinball machines and video games a few years ago. The collection outgrew their home, so they opened it up to the community. Eric keeps the machines running; Erin runs the business.
The name is a nod to the Savannah River Site, which produced material for nuclear weapons until the end of the Cold War and is such a big part of Aiken’s story. And it’s catchy.
list: Visitors come from across SC and Georgia

items.a: No, but anyone under 18 must be with an adult at all times. Some games have flashing lights or adult themes, so parental caution is advised.

items.q: Can I leave and come back?
items.a: Yes. All-day passes come with a wristband. A one-hour pass expires an hour after purchase, and if we’re at capacity when you return you may need to wait.

We’re on the ground floor of the Holley Building, with ramps at both ends of the block and a concrete floor. We have 26″ and 30″ stools and 4″ steps, and we’re testing lower pinball legs for wheelchair users.
Parking is free in downtown Aiken, with more beside the SRP Bank on Hayne Avenue.
Sorry, no pets: we have severe pet allergies, and some machines are loud enough to upset animals.
